lineage: No in-house locker (used HelloKitty/FiveHands, Zeppelin, BlackCat, Quantum); operators moved to Rhysida RaaS in 2023 and are tracked by Microsoft as Vanilla Tempest
summary: Vice Society is an intrusion, exfiltration and extortion crew that first appeared in mid-2021 and focused heavily on the education and healthcare sectors. It gets in with valid VPN credentials (often without MFA) or through exploited internet-facing systems. It then escalates with public exploits such as PrintNightmare, Zerologon and CLFS, persists with SystemBC and PortStarter, and steals large data sets with a custom PowerShell uploader and MegaSync/Rclone before deploying a rented or borrowed encryptor. In 2025 the same operators (Vanilla Tempest) delivered the Oyster backdoor through SEO-poisoned fake Microsoft Teams installers that were signed with fraudulently obtained certificates, then deployed Rhysida.
uniqueTraits: Uses public privilege-escalation exploits very soon after access: PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675/34527), CLFS CVE-2022-24521 and Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472)
SystemBC PowerShell loader persisted through a Run key value named 'socks'; PortStarter Go backdoor persisted through scheduled tasks 'System' and '_SystemCheck_' and opened firewall ports
Custom PowerShell exfiltration script (w1.ps1) that picks files by keyword and uploads them over HTTP POST, built only from native cmdlets
Mass password resets of victim accounts (more than 150,000 users in one case) to lock out defenders
2025: fake MSTeamsSetup.exe installers reached through SEO poisoning, signed with Trusted Signing, SSL.com, DigiCert and GlobalSign certificates, delivering Oyster and then Rhysida

chain.procedure: Logs in to the victim VPN with valid credentials, presumed bought from an initial access broker, on accounts that have no MFA.
chain.noAtomicReason: The login happens at the VPN perimeter with purchased credentials. No endpoint atomic reproduces it, so validate it with VPN and IdP logon analytics instead.

chain.procedure: 2025 Vanilla Tempest campaign: SEO poisoning leads users to lookalike domains (for example teams-download[.]buzz). There they download and run a fake MSTeamsSetup.exe that is signed with a fraudulently obtained certificate and loads the Oyster backdoor.

atomics.note: Runs a downloaded, potentially unwanted installer-style executable. This exercises the user-launched download telemetry but does not use a signed Teams lookalike.

chain.techniqueName: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
chain.procedure: SystemBC is launched by a PowerShell script (svchost.ps1) and kept alive through a Run key value named 'socks'.

atomics.note: Writes a Run key value that launches a payload, matching the SystemBC 'socks' Run-key persistence.
PowerShell-written RunOnce key, a variant of the same autostart location.

chain.procedure: The PortStarter backdoor is persisted with scheduled tasks named 'System' and '_SystemCheck_'.

atomics.note: Creates a local scheduled task with schtasks, as PortStarter does.
The same task created through the PowerShell cmdlets.

chain.procedure: PortStarter changes Windows firewall settings and opens ports so it can reach its C2 servers.

atomics.testName: Open a local port through Windows Firewall to any profile
atomics.note: Opens a local port through Windows Firewall, the same change PortStarter makes.

atomics.testName: Allow Executable Through Firewall Located in Non-Standard Location
atomics.note: Allows an executable in a non-standard path through the firewall.

chain.procedure: Exploits PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675 / CVE-2021-34527) and the CLFS driver flaw CVE-2022-24521 locally, and runs Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) against domain controllers soon after gaining access.
chain.noAtomicReason: The local catalogue has no PrintNightmare, CLFS or Zerologon exploitation test, and exploit code is out of scope. Use vulnerability-management data plus Spooler and Netlogon (event 5829) analytics instead.

chain.procedure: Runs Advanced IP Scanner and Advanced Port Scanner, plus custom PowerShell discovery scripts, to map the network.

atomics.note: PowerShell /24 port sweep, which produces the same burst of internal connection attempts as the GUI scanners.
Nmap port scan as a scanner-tool stand-in.

chain.procedure: Dumps LSASS with comsvcs.dll MiniDump through rundll32 instead of Mimikatz.

atomics.note: Dumps LSASS memory with comsvcs.dll MiniDump, the procedure Microsoft reported.

chain.procedure: On a domain controller, runs ntdsutil to make a full ntds.dit backup in a folder named temp_l0gs, and uses secretsdump to extract AD hashes.

atomics.testName: Dump Active Directory Database with NTDSUtil
atomics.note: Dumps the AD database with ntdsutil IFM, the Sophos-observed procedure.

atomics.testName: Create Volume Shadow Copy with vssadmin
atomics.note: Creates a volume shadow copy with vssadmin, the same NTDS-theft goal through a different path.

chain.techniqueName: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
chain.procedure: Runs PowerSploit Invoke-Kerberoast to request service tickets for offline cracking.

atomics.note: Requests service tickets with Invoke-Kerberoast from PowerShell.
Requests all SPN tickets through native PowerShell.

chain.procedure: Turns off Microsoft Defender Antivirus with registry commands and removes security programs with WMIC.

atomics.note: Turns off Defender through registry values.
Uninstalls an application with WMIC, the same mechanism used to remove security programs.

chain.procedure: Stages scripts and the ransomware on hidden '$' shares, then runs them remotely with PsExec and Impacket wmiexec/atexec. Ransomware is also pushed out through Group Policy.

atomics.testName: Copy and Execute File with PsExec
atomics.note: Copies a file to an admin share and runs it with PsExec.
Impacket wmiexec.py remote execution.
at.exe task creation, which approximates the scheduled-task telemetry Impacket atexec leaves.

chain.procedure: Installs AnyDesk silently on multiple systems from the command line as the main remote-access channel.

atomics.testName: AnyDesk Files Detected Test on Windows
atomics.note: Downloads and runs AnyDesk on the host.

chain.procedure: A custom PowerShell script (w1.ps1) picks directories by keyword with Get-ChildItem/Select-String and uploads files to Vice Society servers over HTTP POST, running up to 10 concurrent jobs.

atomics.note: PowerShell sends staged data out over HTTP to a C2 endpoint, like the w1.ps1 upload loop.
HTTP upload of staged data over an unencrypted channel.

chain.techniqueName: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
chain.procedure: Compresses data with 7-Zip and uploads it to cloud storage with MegaSync and Rclone, sometimes reaching hundreds of GB. WinSCP is also used.

atomics.testName: Exfiltrate data with rclone to cloud Storage - Mega (Windows)
atomics.note: Uploads data to MEGA with rclone.

atomics.testName: Compress Data and lock with password for Exfiltration with 7zip
atomics.note: Builds a password-protected 7-Zip archive before exfiltration.

chain.procedure: Scripts reset the passwords of victim accounts, including email accounts and in one case more than 150,000 users, to lock out legitimate users during extortion.

atomics.note: Changes a Windows user's password from the command line.

chain.procedure: Deletes Windows Server shadow copies with vssadmin, and deletes backups and Mongo databases with WMIC.

atomics.note: vssadmin delete shadows.

atomics.testName: Windows - Delete Volume Shadow Copies via WMI
atomics.note: Shadow-copy deletion through WMI.

chain.procedure: Deploys HelloKitty/FiveHands, Zeppelin (Vice Society-branded .v-society) and later Rhysida (.rhysida, CriticalBreachDetected.pdf), plus a Linux ESXi encryptor. Binaries are pushed with PsExec.

atomics.note: Drops a ransom note artifact. The Vice Society/Rhysida encryptor itself is not reproduced.
Encrypts test files with GPG4Win to generate bulk file-encryption telemetry.
